extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark comprising 20,000 self-contradictory instructions, evenly split between language-language (L-L) and vision-language (V-L) paradigms across 8 tasks, designed to evaluate the capability of large multimodal models (LMMs) to recognize conflicting commands.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate, which leverages programs and large language models in a multimodal cyclic generation process (language and visual loops comprising Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner) initialized from task-relevant seeds, with quality checking by human experts and LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Task-relevant seed pools, synthetic texts generated via LLMs, programmatically plotted charts and geometric shapes, text-rendered images, and real-world images from the ImageNet dataset (specifically ImageNet-1k validation set for SemanticConflict).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For V-L conflicts, image captions and questions are modified to introduce conflicts. In FigureConflict, numerical data dictionaries are tampered by altering maximum values to minimum values before plotting. In GeometricConflict, descriptions of geometric attributes are swapped to describe non-existent objects. In SemanticConflict, ground-truth ImageNet class names in generated questions are substituted with similar but incorrect object names.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The Cleaner component of AutoCreate excludes generated data that does not meet established quality standards, followed by a quality double-check involving human experts and LLMs before refining new seeds.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Subsets SCI-Core (1%) and SCI-Base (10%) were manually selected by human experts according to the occurring frequency of conflict types and diversity requirements. Model evaluation annotations (hit ratios) were performed by human experts as well as LLM evaluation agents using a uniform evaluation prompt.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate were measured between the LLM evaluation agent (GPT-4) and human expert annotations on vision-language conflicts (e.g., Spearman's rho between 0.854 and 0.999; concordance between 94% and 99%).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Provides a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies, particularly for language beginners and vulnerable populations. Facilitates the creation of diverse instruction datasets and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms (excluding other modalities); lacks fine-grained control to determine conflict degree; does not provide a detailed study on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to recognize and handle self-contradictory instructions.
